0: According to the Bible, who built an ark to escape the Flood?
Note: he brought his family and pairs of animals on board (Genesis 6–9).
1: According to the Bible, which young shepherd defeated the giant Goliath?
Note: he brought him down with a stone from his sling (1 Samuel 17).
2: According to the Book of Jonah, what swallowed the prophet Jonah?
Note: the text speaks of a “great fish”, often pictured as a whale (Jonah 2).
3: According to the Bible, how many commandments did God give to Moses?
Note: they are also called the Decalogue (Exodus 20).
4: According to Genesis, what is the name of the garden where Adam and Eve lived?
Note: it is also called the earthly paradise (Genesis 2).
5: According to Exodus, which sea did Moses part so the Hebrews could cross it?
Note: the Hebrews were fleeing Egypt and Pharaoh's army (Exodus 14).
6: According to Exodus, on which mountain did Moses receive the Tablets of the Law?
Note: Deuteronomy also calls this mountain Horeb (Exodus 19–20).
7: According to Genesis, which son of Jacob was sold by his brothers and later became governor of Egypt?
Note: he was known for interpreting dreams, including Pharaoh's (Genesis 37–41).
8: According to Genesis, which son of Adam and Eve killed his brother Abel?
Note: it is the first murder told in the Bible (Genesis 4).
9: Which king of Israel, famous for his wisdom, built the first Temple in Jerusalem?
Note: his judgement between 2 women fighting over a baby is still famous (1 Kings 3).
10: According to the Book of Daniel, into what pit was the prophet Daniel thrown?
Note: according to the story, an angel shut the lions' mouths and Daniel came out unharmed (Daniel 6).
11: What Greek name is given to the first 5 books of the Bible?
Note: it runs from Genesis to Deuteronomy; “penta” means 5 in Greek.
12: According to Genesis, who lived 969 years, the longest life in the Bible?
13: Which book of the Bible has the most chapters, with 150?
Note: they are songs and prayers, many of them attributed to King David.
14: According to the Gospels, in which town was Jesus born?
Note: Jesus then grew up in Nazareth, in Galilee (Matthew 2, Luke 2).
15: According to the Gospels, what was the name of Jesus' mother?
Note: her husband, Joseph, is described as a carpenter (Matthew 13).
16: According to the Gospels, how many apostles did Jesus choose?
Note: their names are listed in Matthew 10 and Luke 6, among others.
17: According to the Gospel of Luke, where did Mary lay Jesus just after he was born?
Note: there was no room for them in the inn (Luke 2).
18: According to the Gospels, in which river was Jesus baptised?
Note: he was baptised by John the Baptist (Mark 1).
19: According to the Gospel of Matthew, what guided the Magi to Jesus?
Note: the Magi came from the East and offered gold, frankincense and myrrh (Matthew 2).
20: According to the Gospel of John, what was Jesus' first miracle, at the wedding at Cana?
Note: John calls it “the first of the signs” of Jesus (John 2).
21: According to the Gospel of Matthew, for how many pieces of silver did Judas betray Jesus?
Note: regretting what he had done, Judas later gave the money back (Matthew 26–27).
22: According to the Gospels, which apostle denied Jesus 3 times before the rooster crowed?
Note: Jesus had foretold it at his last meal (Matthew 26).
23: According to the Gospel of Luke, which angel told Mary she would be the mother of Jesus?
Note: this event is called the Annunciation (Luke 1).
24: According to the Gospel of John, which friend of Jesus was brought back to life in Bethany?
Note: Lazarus was the brother of Martha and Mary (John 11).
25: According to Matthew and Luke, which king ruled Judea when Jesus was born?
Note: he is known as Herod the Great (Matthew 2, Luke 1).
26: According to the Gospels, what is the name of the place where Jesus was crucified?
Note: the name means “place of the Skull”, Calvary in Latin (John 19).
27: According to the Gospel of Luke, on the road to which village did the risen Jesus appear to 2 disciples?
Note: they only recognised him when he broke the bread (Luke 24).
28: According to the Gospels, what was the apostle Peter's job before he followed Jesus?
Note: he fished on Lake Tiberias, also called the Sea of Galilee (Mark 1).
29: What is the head of the Catholic Church, the Bishop of Rome, called?
Note: the word comes from the Greek “pappas”, meaning “dad”.
30: In which city is Vatican City located?
Note: it is the smallest country in the world, entirely surrounded by Rome.
31: Which sacrament, celebrated with water, marks the start of Christian life?
Note: it can be done by immersion or by pouring water over the head.
32: What do you call the man who celebrates Mass in a Catholic parish?
Note: when he is in charge of a parish, he is also called the parish priest.
33: How many Gospels are there in the New Testament?
Note: they are those of Matthew, Mark, Luke and John.
34: According to the Gospels, what was Matthew's job before he became an apostle?
Note: he is also called Levi in the Gospels of Mark and Luke (Matthew 9).
35: According to the Acts of the Apostles, which city was Saul, the future Saint Paul, heading for when he was converted?
Note: blinded by a light, he could not see for 3 days (Acts 9).
36: How many sacraments does the Catholic Church have?
Note: baptism, confirmation, the Eucharist, reconciliation, anointing of the sick, holy orders and marriage.
37: What is the name of the gathering of cardinals that elects a pope?
Note: white smoke rises from the Sistine Chapel when a pope has been elected.
38: What is the last book of the Christian Bible?
Note: it is also called the Apocalypse, from a Greek word meaning “revelation”.
39: According to the Acts of the Apostles, which disciple was chosen to replace Judas among the 12 apostles?
Note: he was chosen by drawing lots (Acts 1).
40: According to the Acts of the Apostles, who is considered the first Christian martyr?
Note: he was stoned to death in Jerusalem (Acts 7).
41: Which apostle, Peter's brother, is the patron saint of Scotland?
Note: the X-shaped cross on the Scottish flag is called the Saint Andrew's Cross, or Saltire.
42: On what date do most Churches celebrate Christmas?
Note: some Orthodox Churches celebrate it on 7 January, because they follow the Julian calendar.
43: Which Christian feast celebrates the resurrection of Jesus?
Note: it is the most important feast of the Christian calendar.
44: What is the gesture of touching your forehead, chest and both shoulders while praying called?
Note: Catholics and Orthodox Christians both make it, but they touch the shoulders in a different order.
45: In Belgian and French tradition, who brings back the chocolate eggs from Rome and hides them in gardens?
Note: church bells fall silent from Holy Thursday until Easter, hence the idea that they “fly to Rome”.
46: Which tree is traditionally decorated at Christmas?
Note: this tradition spread from Alsace and Germany.
47: Which feast on 1 November honours all the saints?
Note: in many countries it is a public holiday, when families visit graves.
48: How many days does Lent traditionally last?
Note: it recalls the 40 days Jesus spent in the desert (Matthew 4).
49: What is the period of about 4 weeks leading up to Christmas called?
Note: the Advent calendar helps children count down the days to Christmas.
50: Which January feast celebrates the Magi's visit to Jesus?
Note: in Belgium and France, people share a king cake, with a hidden charm inside.
51: Which feast, 50 days after Easter, celebrates the Holy Spirit coming down on the apostles?
Note: its name comes from the Greek “pentekoste”, meaning “fiftieth” (Acts 2).
52: What is the Sunday before Easter called, recalling Jesus' entry into Jerusalem?
Note: according to the Gospels, the crowd waved branches to welcome him (John 12).
53: What is the day that marks the start of Lent for Catholics called?
Note: the priest marks a cross of ashes on the foreheads of the faithful.
54: Which feast celebrates Jesus rising up into heaven?
Note: it falls on a Thursday, 40 days after Easter (Acts 1).
55: Which Catholic feast on 15 August celebrates Mary being taken up into heaven?
Note: on the same day, Orthodox Christians celebrate the Dormition of Mary.
56: Which famous Gothic cathedral stands on the Île de la Cité in Paris?
57: What do you call men who live in a religious community in a monastery?
Note: the word comes from the Greek “monachos”, meaning “solitary”.
58: Which saint, a bishop of Myra, inspired the character of Santa Claus?
Note: his feast day is 6 December, celebrated especially in Belgium, northern France and the Netherlands.
59: Which young heroine of the Hundred Years' War, later made a saint, was burned at Rouen in 1431?
Note: she was canonised by the Catholic Church in 1920.
60: What are the coloured glass windows that decorate churches called?
Note: in the Middle Ages, they told Bible stories in pictures.
61: Which 13th-century Italian saint, known for his love of animals, was born in Assisi?
Note: he founded the Franciscan order and lived in great poverty.
62: Which Roman emperor granted Christians freedom of worship with the Edict of Milan in 313?
Note: he made this decision together with Licinius, emperor of the Roman East.
63: Which German monk published his 95 Theses in 1517, starting the Protestant Reformation?
Note: he also translated the Bible into German.
64: In what language were the texts of the New Testament originally written?
Note: Greek was then the common language of the eastern Roman Empire.
65: Which artist painted the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel in the Vatican?
Note: he worked on it from 1508 to 1512; it includes the famous Creation of Adam.
66: Which architectural style, born in France in the 12th century, is typical of Chartres Cathedral?
Note: it is recognisable by its pointed arches, high vaults and large windows.
67: In which city was the first ecumenical council of Christian history held, in 325?
Note: it drew up the first version of the Creed, a profession of faith still recited today.
68: In what year is the Great Schism between the Eastern and Western Churches usually dated?
Note: since then it has divided the Catholic Church and the Orthodox Church.
69: Which saint translated the Bible into Latin in the version known as the Vulgate?
Note: he worked on it in the late 4th and early 5th centuries, partly in Bethlehem.
